items.headline: Foreigners make record withdrawal from Taiwan stocks on AI rout
items.summary: Overseas investors sold a net $31.78 billion of Taiwanese shares in October, a record, as a global AI selloff pushed the benchmark toward correction. The outflow signals growing investor caution about stretched AI valuations across chip-heavy markets.

items.headline: Macquarie executive says AI will fast-track junior analyst careers
items.summary: Christina Lee, who heads research and sales in Asia at Macquarie Capital, said AI tools may accelerate entry-level analysts' learning curves rather than eliminate their jobs. The comments reframe the AI-jobs debate within Wall Street's advisory and research functions.

items.headline: OpenAI raises less than half of $30 billion funding target
items.summary: OpenAI has secured roughly $11 billion of its initial $30 billion goal as market jitters over the AI trade dampened investor appetite, valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The shortfall signals cooling enthusiasm for even the industry's biggest names.

items.headline: Wall Street starts to call the shots in AI build-out
items.summary: Lenders and investors are demanding tougher terms as the AI infrastructure boom faces a shortage of cheap capital, signaling a new phase in the build-out. Concerns include project delays and a grassroots political backlash against data centers.

items.headline: HSBC to open Hong Kong AI Institute after Singapore launch
items.summary: HSBC announced plans to open an AI Institute in Hong Kong, following its earlier launch in Singapore, to deepen the bank's artificial intelligence capabilities. The move underscores accelerating AI investment among major global financial institutions.

items.headline: AI talent war spreads to Wall Street trading firms
items.summary: Quantitative trading firms are competing with AI labs for top scientists, with first-year compensation for some PhDs reaching as much as $800,000. Firms are using fellowships, university sponsorships and recruiting events to counter AI companies' lucrative offers.

items.headline: China's embodied AI firms raise $13 billion in H1 2026
items.summary: Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the prior year's amount. The surge reflects an intensifying race to give humanoid robots sophisticated 'brains' after mastering physical movement.

items.headline: Santander says AI generated €194 million in business value
items.summary: Spanish banking giant Santander reported that AI initiatives generated €194 million ($216 million) in business value in the first nine months of 2026. CFO José García Cantera said AI is now directly contributing to both revenue and cost reductions across the bank's processes.

items.headline: The tangled web of circular AI financing raises stock fears
items.summary: Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom acted as $5 billion cornerstone investors in Meta's $25 billion stock sale, deepening the circular financing underpinning AI. The arrangement has stoked concerns about the scale of capital needed for AI infrastructure as tech stocks stumbled.

items.headline: AI investors race to insure the biggest market bet in history
items.summary: Some Wall Street investors are seeking protection against a potential AI downturn, hedging a multitrillion-dollar bet that has lifted stocks from chipmakers to utilities. The scramble for insurance signals growing anxiety beneath the AI-driven market rally.

items.headline: Fortune 500 companies deepen AI adoption but lag on governance
items.summary: A Credo AI study found that while 60% of organizations now deploy AI company-wide, only 4% govern those deployments across the organization. The gap highlights rising enterprise AI adoption outpacing risk management and regulatory compliance frameworks.

items.headline: CNBC Technology Summit highlights AI across sports and retail
items.summary: Executives from Brooklyn Sports, Levi Strauss, Cisco and others discussed AI's expanding role in fan engagement, shopping, and enterprise security at CNBC's 2026 summit. The event spotlighted how AI agents and tools are being embedded across diverse industries.

items.headline: AI reshapes cyber threat landscape with faster, smarter attacks
items.summary: Cybersecurity data in 2026 reveals AI is transforming cyberattacks by increasing their speed, scale and sophistication. The trend raises the stakes for defenders as autonomous AI agents introduce new corporate security risks.

items.headline: Fortune analysts debate whether Anthropic IPO is a good buy
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 reveals a controversial 'Class F' share structure giving its seven co-founders 50.1% of the vote even after selling most of their stakes. The unusual governance setup has sparked debate over investor control ahead of the landmark IPO.

items.headline: Anthropic targets November IPO ahead of Thanksgiving
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 sets up a public market debut as soon as the week before Thanksgiving, later than its originally expected October timeline. The shift lets the AI firm share third-quarter financials with potential investors amid debate over AI pacing.

items.headline: Anthropic files for one of the biggest IPOs in history
items.summary: Anthropic's prospectus revealed revenue jumped to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, a 1,300% year-over-year increase driven by Claude. The company committed over $269 billion in combined compute spending with Microsoft, Google and Amazon.

items.headline: Anthropic's compute bills expose customer-concentration risk
items.summary: Anthropic's S-1 shows it is on the hook for billions in compute commitments while its usage-based customers can walk away at any time. The disclosure highlights the financial fragility beneath the AI leader's explosive revenue growth.

items.headline: Anthropic going public raises stakes for entire AI industry
items.summary: Valued near $1 trillion and backed by over $130 billion in funding, Anthropic could raise $100 billion and become one of the world's biggest public companies. It sits atop a pyramid of suppliers whose heavy AI spending hinges on sustained demand.

items.headline: Meta launches Muse Wonder models to rival Anthropic, OpenAI
items.summary: Meta unveiled a new series of AI models called Muse Wonder, which it says has caught up to leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. CEO Mark Zuckerberg and AI chief Alexandr Wang promoted the larger, more capable models on social media.

items.headline: ServiceNow stock slides as earnings miss clouds AI outlook
items.summary: ServiceNow shares fell after a quarterly earnings miss overshadowed its raised artificial intelligence outlook. The reaction underscores investor sensitivity to AI monetization even at enterprise software leaders with strong AI momentum.
